sonnet.problem: The answer is already given by earlier cards. Card 13 has David say 'Return the ark of God to the city.' Card 14's question states 'David sends the ark of God back to Jerusalem.' Card 16 has David send Zadok and Abiathar back to the city. The True/False card then asks the same fact again, so it tests nothing new.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. Once a choice has been answered, the cards after it can build on that answer. An easy follow-up is fine. For example, once the baker knows the greater light rules the day, a card can ask whether the lesser light rules the night. An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact. Two lines that make the same point get one question.
